newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai insurance licences to spark competition.
newsitem.headline: New Thai insurance licences to spark competition.

text.p: Existing small and family-run Thai insurance firms would need to re-engineer their businesses after the government on Tuesday approved 28 new local insurance licences, a Phatra Insurance Plc executive said.
Pongsak Manasirisuk, first senior vice president of Phatra Insurance, told Reuters that existing insurance firms would need to work harder in the face of anticipated stiffer competition.
"They have to re-engineer their businesses otherwise they'll have to sell their licences," he said.
The Thai cabinet approved 12 new life and 16 non-life insurance licences to locally incorporated firms.
Pongsak said it would be beneficial to the non-life insurance industry if the 16 new licence holders entered into businesses that had not yet been undertaken.
"Non-life insurance premiums at the end of 1995 amounted to about 52 billion baht ($2 billion) and I think it's good to have more competitors in the market," he added.
